title: Private contact orchestration composition boundary
purpose: Introduce the provider-neutral server-side composition seam required for the canonical private insurance contact route while preserving fail-closed behavior until an outbound provider is explicitly configured in a later authorized slice.

currentState.routeBehavior: POST-only, same-origin protected, validates canonical provider-neutral contact request, requires RIVER_CRM_DB, loads canonical relationship, then returns HTTP 503 because provider composition is intentionally unavailable.
currentState.orchestration: src/lib/insurance/contact-orchestration.ts already owns relationship resolution, server-side destination resolution, current consent/suppression evaluation, durable queued and attempting contact-attempt persistence, provider invocation, canonical provider failure persistence, and idempotency.
currentState.identity: Contact attempt IDs and idempotency keys remain canonical domain identities; server UUID generation may follow existing River OS crypto.randomUUID() precedent.
currentState.providerState: No canonical outbound Telnyx runtime configuration contract exists; Telnyx provider activation remains outside this slice.

composition.goal: Make route-level orchestration composition explicit and testable without activating any real outbound provider.
requirements: Keep the route provider-agnostic: no Telnyx, Twilio, RingCentral, OpenPhone, Plivo, Vonage, fetch, axios, provider credentials, or provider-specific environment reads in insurance-contact.ts.
Reuse createInsuranceContactOrchestrationService rather than duplicating eligibility, consent, destination, persistence, provider-result, or idempotency policy in the route.
Reuse canonical River CRM, CRM-growth, and contact-attempt D1 persistence factories.
Keep outbound provider resolution behind one server-side composition boundary.
When no provider composition is available, fail closed before orchestration creates or mutates a contact attempt and preserve an explicit HTTP 503 response.
Do not accept destination, phone, email, provider, provider reference, credentials, attempt state, timestamps, or idempotency identity directly from browser form data.
A later explicitly authorized provider-activation slice may supply a concrete provider to this seam; INS-007T itself must not make network requests or activate Telnyx.

failureMapping: provider composition unavailable -> 503 before contact-attempt persistence/provider invocation
routeContract.note: Do not invent success redirects or UI controls in this slice until a provider is explicitly authorized.

tests: Provider-unavailable composition returns fail-closed result without provider invocation or attempt write.
Composition uses canonical D1 relationship, CRM-growth consent, and contact-attempt persistence dependencies.
Route remains POST-only and same-origin protected.
Route continues to reject browser-supplied destination/phone/email/provider data.
Route contains no provider SDK, Telnyx-specific composition, direct fetch, or outbound credential access.
Existing contact-orchestration domain tests remain authoritative for eligibility, suppression, provider-failure, persistence, and idempotency semantics.
boundaries: No live phone call, SMS, or email.
No Telnyx provider activation or credential configuration.
No contact UI button or dialing controls.
No routing, lead scoring, or automatic producer assignment.
Do not weaken INS-007S read-only contact-attempt presentation or INS-007R view-context preservation.
